system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer review — Wattlebridge Holdings.** The Seller’s “[STANDARD]” labels and efficiency note do not establish buyer agreement. All positions remain subject to review. The recommendations below are proposed buyer positions, not previously agreed terms; underlying DD documents and the complete SPA have not been provided.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A higher general cap, with separate protection for fundamental, tax, specific-indemnity and fraud claims. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and recoverability; 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, with only the excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims; no thresholds for fundamental, tax or specific-indemnity claims. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**; the Seller’s combined thresholds materially erode recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General warranties: notice within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, separate category-specific periods and preservation of claims notified in time. | **Seek 24–36 months and reject automatic extension across claim categories**; latent issues may emerge after the first post-Completion reporting cycle. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and time limits. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, authority, ownership, valid issue, all shares and freedom from encumbrances; no basket/de minimis. | **Seek a 100% price cap and six-year contractual claim period**, subject to applicable law; ownership and authority are core acquisition risks, not ordinary business warranties. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | No express fraud exception is shown; limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims. | Express preservation of claims and remedies for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation, including attributable conduct by Seller representatives. | **Carve fraud out of caps, thresholds, contractual time bars, disclosure/knowledge defences and remedy restrictions**; the Seller must not contractually shelter fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of indexed data-room materials, referenced matters, accounts, registers and public records. | Only fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter, against identified warranties; a frozen, accessible disclosure bundle. | **Reject blanket/deemed disclosure and require specific, fair disclosure**, with any general disclosures narrowly agreed; document availability is not meaningful disclosure of every associated risk. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including matters merely discoverable from data rooms or public records. | No knowledge bar; alternatively, actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer personnel only, without imputation or a duty to investigate. | **Delete constructive and adviser knowledge; preserve specific indemnities regardless of knowledge**; diligence should not transfer undisclosed risk to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent, despite outstanding evidence of consent and associated conditions. | A Completion condition requiring valid consent, satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions and no materially adverse contractual changes, waivable only by Buyer. | **Require substantive satisfaction before Completion, not delivery alone**; approximately 30% of FY26 revenue depends on this relationship. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Repayment through Completion funds flow at Seller’s economic cost, with binding payoff arrangements and releases effective at Completion. | **Require simultaneous discharge/release mechanics, including all relevant security and guarantees**; a debt-free acquisition cannot leave the Buyer exposed to Seller-era secured debt. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Express Seller allocation, quantified payroll tax/superannuation/other applicable on-costs, and payment or price adjustment plus protection for residual liabilities. | **Include bonuses and applicable on-costs in funds flow/debt-like adjustments without double counting**; omission could leave the Buyer funding transaction-triggered liabilities. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 recorded open, without verified payment or confirmatory assignment. | Evidence of cleared payment and effective IP transfer before Completion; a broader specific indemnity for pre-Completion ownership/assignment defects and resulting losses. | **Require payment verification, effective assignment and an indemnity outside general warranty limitations**; paying the invoice alone may not resolve chain-of-title or third-party claims. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope, notification obligations and loss remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, evidence preservation, containment, legal assessment of notification duties, updates and a specific indemnity for the pre-Completion incident. | **Require an agreed response plan and tailored indemnity, with Completion protection if findings warrant it**; uncertainty is neither proof of a notifiable breach nor evidence of immateriality. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling **AUD 330,000** characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Review the related commitments together for timing, scope, termination rights, accruals, authorisation and pricing treatment. | **Reserve classification pending DD-008/DD-011 review; adjust price or require consent if warranted**; neither ordinary-course treatment nor debt-like treatment is established by the disclosed facts. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance sweep across all Claims. | Expressly separate general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax covenant/indemnity, specific indemnities, covenants and price/debt adjustments, with clear priority rules. | **Replace the catch-all regime with category-specific provisions and express exceptions**; otherwise general limitations can silently defeat specially negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012’s share register showing Harbourglass holds 100%. | Independent verification of issued capital, ownership history, encumbrances, options/convertibles and transfer restrictions, plus valid Completion transfer deliverables. | **Verify title beyond the register and retain robust title warranties and clean-title Completion requirements**; the register alone does not establish unencumbered, transferable ownership of all equity. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties said to be settled under the general regime. | Tax warranties plus a pre-Completion tax indemnity with appropriate exclusions and conduct provisions; substantive IP ownership, licensing, infringement and assignment protection. | **Reopen both: seek tax protection for seven years or longer where relevant assessment exposure requires, and a separately negotiated IP cap/survival regime**; neither category should be deemed settled or compressed into the general package. |

**Priority:** Do not complete without effective Bluefen consent and associated conditions, Riverlark repayment/release arrangements, agreed bonus allocation and satisfactory resolution of Ironquay IP ownership. The export incident requires urgent investigation rather than an assumed legal conclusion.
=== END ADVICE ===
